sections.heading: Pros
Cons
Review
sections.text: Luuk Herssen is a 5-star Spectro Gauntlets Main DPS character whose kit revolves around aerial combat and building up to his very strong single-hit Ultimate nuke. Luuk’s best combat playstyle is to attack enemies in mid-air to build up his enhanced skills to eventually lead to an enhanced plunging attack which will empower his Ultimate by a massive amount, which he can then unleash on the enemies for a massive blast of damage (it is indeed one of the strongest Ultimate nukes in the game by far, competing with characters like Aemeath with her second Ultimate and Jinhsi’s Skill). Let’s look into the specifics of how to make that happen:

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
sections.text:
Luuk’s most important mechanic to keep in mind when rotating by far is his Golden Rule mechanic. This is a kind of buff related to Luuk that’s given to other teammates on a 24-second cooldown following his Intro. It is, in fact, triggered by his Intro and will cause him to start with a full Forte bar when rotating. This is extremely important and vital to his rotation, as he needs to consume his Forte bar to use his enhanced Skills, which enhance his Ultimate’s damage multiplier, allow him to access his special plunging attack called “Gavel of Earthshaker” and also increase the damage of that same plunging attack. Overall, it’s very important to keep in mind Luuk will only ever rotate on this 24-second cooldown basis (although realistically it’ll be a 25-second cooldown instead since that’s his Ultimate’s cooldown duration). It also gives him the extra Concerto needed to get his Outro off after performing his full rotation, so overall it’s very important to keep in mind that Luuk operates on the cooldown of Golden Rule.
 Other than this, his most important mechanic is that in order to empower his Ultimate, he needs to cast 3 enhanced skills that he gets by consuming his Forte; in order, they are Ring, Breach and Glare. Glare also allows him to cast his Gavel of Earthshaker plunging attack, which deals a lot of damage on its own, so most of Luuk’s damage is locked behind actually casting those 3 Skills. He accesses them by casting 3 mid-air attacks consecutively. All 3 skills provide a total of 75% multiplier increase to his Ultimate, which, as you can probably guess, is huge.
 In other words, by these factors alone, it is very easy to guess Luuk’s kit summarizes to every 25 seconds, cast his Intro and do a rotation composed of 3 strings of 3 mid-air attacks, 3 skills, a plunging attack and finish it off with his Ultimate. But you can optimize a bit further by looking into the finer details of his kit, so let’s have a look at that.

sections.heading: Rotation Details
sections.text:
Luuk possesses 2 different strings of Mid-air Attacks that he can use. One is his Dissection string activated by pressing Basic, and the other is his Resection string activated by pressing Jump. Which one is better? While the Basic string is very slightly shorter (by a difference of a few frames), the Jump string deals slightly more damage per rotation and generates slightly more Energy. Overall, the Jump string is hence slightly better for total damage per rotation and even considering the extra time, that makes it the better one to use generally.
 Additionally, after he casts his Ring and Breach skills, he also gains access to a special Basic Attack called Golden Impale. While this sounds good on paper, it doesn’t deal more damage than even his 3rd Mid-air Attack, which is actually really low amounts of damage. The animation, on the other hand, takes a while to execute and can make his rotations really tight for buff uptime purposes. For this reason, since we have to cast Golden Impale to access his next Mid-air Attack string following the Golden Impale cast, it’s optimal to cast it and then dash out of it in order to access the next Mid-air Attack string quicker. This ensures Luuk retains all character buffs in the team throughout his whole rotation (and most importantly his huge Ultimate blast at the end of it) against all kinds of enemies in the game (unless he gets interrupted too much, but dodging out of the way is very much a possibility using this Dash Cancel technique). In the case of Luuk, it’s particularly important to learn for buff uptime reasons - as we said earlier.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
sections.text:
Luuk is overall a very budget-friendly character. While he relies on Tune Strain to activate a lot of his kit’s mechanics and enhance his damage, he can apply it and stack it up fully on his own to a good degree, which makes him very self-sufficient. Other teammates that can play around Tune Strain, such as Denia or Lynae with Mornye, are very strong support choices for him due to these mechanics; however, they’re not strictly necessary for Luuk to operate well. Indeed, Luuk is one of the most accessible characters in the game, since the permanently accessible 5-star weapon Pulsation Bracer plays into his Basic Attack DMG and Tune Strain-focused playstyle, and the free character Sanhua accessed just via logging in for a few days via a beginner event is a perfectly suitable damage booster for him.
 Luuk harbours one of the most accessible playstyles, and while he has limited built-in Interruption Resistance, learning his rotation is not very difficult and he can serve new players as a way to not only get comfortable with team rotations, but his playstyle also heavily incentivizes learning how to dodge out of the way of enemies.
 When it comes to the performance granted by players who pick him up and build a team around him, he doesn’t disappoint, rising up to the standard of other modern DPS just below Aemeath, Hiyuki or Sigrika in his full premium team with Denia and Mornye, and in his more accessible teams he rivals even Carlotta or Zani in their own full premium compositions. However, this is only in single-target scenarios. Luuk’s biggest weakness as a mid-air single-target-oriented damage dealer is multi-wave content, and while Denia helps him by providing constant AoE off-field grouping, without her he is almost completely helpless in AoE-centric content like Whimpering Wastes and even with her he remains barely at the average of most 2.x characters.
 In conclusion, while his multi-wave and AoE capabilities aren’t off the charts, they remain usable (with Denia) and his performance against boss enemies is amazing, so he definitely appears on the list of the strongest DPS characters in the game that you can acquire and perform well with, whether you’re more experienced or more casual. Luuk’s accessibility in both investment and playstyle makes him worth considering for a lot of players, beginners and veterans alike, and his performance results definitely make him worth the investment while not overshadowing other modern DPS releases.

sections.heading: Rotations & Gameplay
sections.text: Luuk wants to use each of his Aureate of Execution Skills after Mid-Air Attacks to gain Endnotes of the Endgame, powering up his Ultimate. These Skills gain a massive damage increase while Ichor Flow is full, as this lets him enter the Aureate Judge state, letting him consume Ichor Flow for damage increases. He has only 1 real rotation with slight deviations.

sections.heading: Echo Timing
sections.text: Generally skip using this as his Skill deals more damage. However, if you have a lot of headroom to Swap Cancel before his rotation starts, you may cast Echo Skill then.

 While it is technically possible to have all buffs active for the entire duration without dash cancelling Golden Impale assuming you have frame perfect inputs, the dash cancel is highly recommended in order to improve Team DPS and to ensure Luuk’s Ultimate is able to retain every buff.
 Additionally, extra Skill and Echo casts can be performed pre-Intro if your team allows for some light amounts of quickswap (though this is really limited and will barely lead to any notable damage increases).

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Denia Lynae Sanhua - The best second slot buffers for Luuk. Denia is the overall strongest due to extra Tune Strain application, massive buffing and personall damage, constant off-field grouping and a fast rotation, all very strong points for Luuk. Lynae provides very valuable extra Tune Strain application while also slighlty increasing Luuk's general DMG Amplification via her Outro on top of her other massive ATK and DMG Bonus buffs, which makes her a good second best choice. Sanhua is however totally fine as a budget option as she is accessible for free and provides a lot of extra Basic DMG Amplification on top of her usual ATK buffs and super fast rotation which makes her a very good choice as well. Keep in mind though that she may require Luuk to extend his rotation with an extra Mid-air Attack chain following his Ultimate in order to ensure he rotates on a 25s cooldown.
 Mornye The Shorekeeper Verina - The best general Supports for Luuk. Mornye is always the strongest since Luuk applies his own Tune Strain for Mornye to bounce off of and buff him to the max of her abilities, even at S0. Shorekeeper and Verina are however always strong alternatives that are competitive if you don't have access to Mornye.

This ensures Luuk retains all character buffs in the team throughout his whole rotation (and most importantly his huge Ultimate blast at the end of it) against all kinds of enemies in the game (unless he gets interrupted too much, but dodging out of the way is very much a possibility using this Dash Cancel technique). In the case of Luuk, it’s particularly important to learn for buff uptime reasons - as we said earlier.

 Pros & Cons
 Pros
 Strong damage in a mid-air combat style, which makes it fairly easy to avoid a good amount of enemy attacks;

 One of the most accessible DPS in the game by far, able to function very well with a permanently obtainable weapon and teammates;

 Super easy to understand, pick up, and optimize. Has one of the lowest barriers to entry in terms of optimization ceiling in the game.

 Review
 Luuk Herssen is a 5-star Spectro Gauntlets Main DPS character whose kit revolves around aerial combat and building up to his very strong single-hit Ultimate nuke. Luuk’s best combat playstyle is to attack enemies in mid-air to build up his enhanced skills to eventually lead to an enhanced plunging attack which will empower his Ultimate by a massive amount, which he can then unleash on the enemies for a massive blast of damage (it is indeed one of the strongest Ultimate nukes in the game by far, competing with characters like Aemeath with her second Ultimate and Jinhsi’s Skill). Let’s look into the specifics of how to make that happen:
 Key Mechanics
 Luuk’s most important mechanic to keep in mind when rotating by far is his Golden Rule mechanic. This is a kind of buff related to Luuk that’s given to other teammates on a 24-second cooldown following his Intro. It is, in fact, triggered by his Intro and will cause him to start with a full Forte bar when rotating. This is extremely important and vital to his rotation, as he needs to consume his Forte bar to use his enhanced Skills, which enhance his Ultimate’s damage multiplier, allow him to access his special plunging attack called “Gavel of Earthshaker” and also increase the damage of that same plunging attack. Overall, it’s very important to keep in mind Luuk will only ever rotate on this 24-second cooldown basis (although realistically it’ll be a 25-second cooldown instead since that’s his Ultimate’s cooldown duration). It also gives him the extra Concerto needed to get his Outro off after performing his full rotation, so overall it’s very important to keep in mind that Luuk operates on the cooldown of Golden Rule.
 Other than this, his most important mechanic is that in order to empower his Ultimate, he needs to cast 3 enhanced skills that he gets by consuming his Forte; in order, they are Ring, Breach and Glare. Glare also allows him to cast his Gavel of Earthshaker plunging attack, which deals a lot of damage on its own, so most of Luuk’s damage is locked behind actually casting those 3 Skills. He accesses them by casting 3 mid-air attacks consecutively. All 3 skills provide a total of 75% multiplier increase to his Ultimate, which, as you can probably guess, is huge.
 In other words, by these factors alone, it is very easy to guess Luuk’s kit summarizes to every 25 seconds, cast his Intro and do a rotation composed of 3 strings of 3 mid-air attacks, 3 skills, a plunging attack and finish it off with his Ultimate. But you can optimize a bit further by looking into the finer details of his kit, so let’s have a look at that.
 Rotation Details
 Luuk possesses 2 different strings of Mid-air Attacks that he can use. One is his Dissection string activated by pressing Basic, and the other is his Resection string activated by pressing Jump. Which one is better? While the Basic string is very slightly shorter (by a difference of a few frames), the Jump string deals slightly more damage per rotation and generates slightly more Energy. Overall, the Jump string is hence slightly better for total damage per rotation and even considering the extra time, that makes it the better one to use generally.
 Additionally, after he casts his Ring and Breach skills, he also gains access to a special Basic Attack called Golden Impale. While this sounds good on paper, it doesn’t deal more damage than even his 3rd Mid-air Attack, which is actually really low amounts of damage. The animation, on the other hand, takes a while to execute and can make his rotations really tight for buff uptime purposes. For this reason, since we have to cast Golden Impale to access his next Mid-air Attack string following the Golden Impale cast, it’s optimal to cast it and then dash out of it in order to access the next Mid-air Attack string quicker. This ensures Luuk retains all character buffs in the team throughout his whole rotation (and most importantly his huge Ultimate blast at the end of it) against all kinds of enemies in the game (unless he gets interrupted too much, but dodging out of the way is very much a possibility using this Dash Cancel technique). In the case of Luuk, it’s particularly important to learn for buff uptime reasons - as we said earlier.
 Meta Position & Conclusion
 Luuk is overall a very budget-friendly character. While he relies on Tune Strain to activate a lot of his kit’s mechanics and enhance his damage, he can apply it and stack it up fully on his own to a good degree, which makes him very self-sufficient. Other teammates that can play around Tune Strain, such as Denia or Lynae with Mornye, are very strong support choices for him due to these mechanics; however, they’re not strictly necessary for Luuk to operate well. Indeed, Luuk is one of the most accessible characters in the game, since the permanently accessible 5-star weapon Pulsation Bracer plays into his Basic Attack DMG and Tune Strain-focused playstyle, and the free character Sanhua accessed just via logging in for a few days via a beginner event is a perfectly suitable damage booster for him.
 Luuk harbours one of the most accessible playstyles, and while he has limited built-in Interruption Resistance, learning his rotation is not very difficult and he can serve new players as a way to not only get comfortable with team rotations, but his playstyle also heavily incentivizes learning how to dodge out of the way of enemies.
 When it comes to the performance granted by players who pick him up and build a team around him, he doesn’t disappoint, rising up to the standard of other modern DPS just below Aemeath, Hiyuki or Sigrika in his full premium team with Denia and Mornye, and in his more accessible teams he rivals even Carlotta or Zani in their own full premium compositions. However, this is only in single-target scenarios. Luuk’s biggest weakness as a mid-air single-target-oriented damage dealer is multi-wave content, and while Denia helps him by providing constant AoE off-field grouping, without her he is almost completely helpless in AoE-centric content like Whimpering Wastes and even with her he remains barely at the average of most 2.x characters.
 In conclusion, while his multi-wave and AoE capabilities aren’t off the charts, they remain usable (with Denia) and his performance against boss enemies is amazing, so he definitely appears on the list of the strongest DPS characters in the game that you can acquire and perform well with, whether you’re more experienced or more casual. Luuk’s accessibility in both investment and playstyle makes him worth considering for a lot of players, beginners and veterans alike, and his performance results definitely make him worth the investment while not overshadowing other modern DPS releases.

 Rotation
 Rotations & Gameplay
 Luuk wants to use each of his Aureate of Execution Skills after Mid-Air Attacks to gain Endnotes of the Endgame, powering up his Ultimate. These Skills gain a massive damage increase while Ichor Flow is full, as this lets him enter the Aureate Judge state, letting him consume Ichor Flow for damage increases. He has only 1 real rotation with slight deviations.

 Generally skip using this as his Skill deals more damage. However, if you have a lot of headroom to Swap Cancel before his rotation starts, you may cast Echo Skill then.

 Synergies
 Denia Lynae Sanhua - The best second slot buffers for Luuk. Denia is the overall strongest due to extra Tune Strain application, massive buffing and personall damage, constant off-field grouping and a fast rotation, all very strong points for Luuk. Lynae provides very valuable extra Tune Strain application while also slighlty increasing Luuk's general DMG Amplification via her Outro on top of her other massive ATK and DMG Bonus buffs, which makes her a good second best choice. Sanhua is however totally fine as a budget option as she is accessible for free and provides a lot of extra Basic DMG Amplification on top of her usual ATK buffs and super fast rotation which makes her a very good choice as well. Keep in mind though that she may require Luuk to extend his rotation with an extra Mid-air Attack chain following his Ultimate in order to ensure he rotates on a 25s cooldown.
 Mornye The Shorekeeper Verina - The best general Supports for Luuk. Mornye is always the strongest since Luuk applies his own Tune Strain for Mornye to bounce off of and buff him to the max of her abilities, even at S0. Shorekeeper and Verina are however always strong alternatives that are competitive if you don't have access to Mornye.
